result.strongest_objection: The design does not provide amortized O(1) prepend under normal persistent-list branching, despite making that its title and primary goal. After one prepend claims a tail's watermark, every later prepend of that same still-live tail loses the CAS and copies the entire tail. Repeating `x :: base` while retaining `base` therefore costs Θ(m·len(base)), and analogous branching affects `++`. The geometric-growth proof covers slack exhaustion along a single linear-use chain, not CAS failures caused by aliases, concurrency, or branching.
result.catch: The document treats loser-copy as a correctness detail but never analyzes its asymptotic conflict with immutable-list reuse. AC-1 through AC-4 and AC-9 test only linear recursive chains, so they cannot validate the advertised general complexity or A9 cost-visibility claim; scheduling and alias topology silently determine whether `::` is O(1) or O(n).
result.proposed_fix: Either narrow the proposal explicitly to “amortized O(1) for unbranched, single-claimer builder chains,” change the title/goals/A9 claim accordingly, document `x :: sharedTail` as O(len(sharedTail)) after the first claim, and add a branching benchmark/acceptance criterion; or, if general amortized O(1) prepend is required, replace Option B with a genuinely persistent representation such as cons cells and plan the accessor/construction-site migration needed to remove direct writable `Elements` access.

result.strongest_objection: The closest concern is a potential escape hatch in the listmut analyzer: R2 explicitly flags the slice passed as a []Value argument or returned, but an AST-based linter might miss the hand-off if the Elements slice is packed into a struct field, captured in a closure, or assigned to an any interface before crossing an un-allowlisted function boundary.
result.catch: Ensure the listmut CI gate is implemented using SSA-based taint tracking (e.g., using golang.org/x/tools/go/ssa) rather than naive AST matching, so intra-procedural taint correctly tracks the slice through wrappers and interface conversions.
result.proposed_fix: Update Phase 3 to explicitly require listmut to use SSA data-flow/taint tracking (via buildssa) to enforce R1 and R2, guaranteeing that assigning the slice to a struct field or interface still triggers an R2 violation if that wrapper escapes to an unaudited callee.
